issues.title: Production notes overstate the available story

The root inventory contains only Chapter 1 prose, fourteen interior page prompts, three cover prompts including the app cover, and supporting notes; no reader image files or second chapter are present.
issues.why: An audit cannot claim coverage of unavailable chapters or assess the ending of a 105-chapter plan as completed fiction.
issues.preserve: Every existing file and the planned second chapter title.
solutions: Recover the claimed originals into a separately inventoried source addition and extend the audit. Risk: further findings may change priorities.
Approve an available-material audit and treat Chapter 2 onward as unwritten or unavailable, with later expansion from approved plans. Risk: recovered material may require reconciliation.
issues.uncertainty: Absence is confirmed only within this story root; files could exist elsewhere. No deletion or loss is inferred.
issues.impact: Rendered continuity and later chapter pacing cannot be reviewed.

Retain Inez only through an explicit rename or separate-character decision with all affected references versioned. Risk: unnecessary cast complexity and divergence from prose.

Approve a deliberate rename and update new versions of every dependent reference. Risk: broad revision for no demonstrated story benefit.

issues.title: The adaptation removes the introduction needed for the name clue
issues.description: The prose introduces Daniel and Tomas by name before Daniel recognizes TOMAS on the door. Pages 5-7 omit that exchange, but Page 7 has Daniel say I FOUND YOUR NAME. Character-lock text is not reader-facing dialogue.
issues.why: Daniel identifies the stranger's name without the scene supplying how he learned it. A fair mystery should preserve this causal link.
issues.preserve: The shock of a scratched future name matching a living person.
solutions: Restore a concise mutual introduction before the scratched-name discussion. Risk: extra lettering requires page rebalance.
Give Tomas an explicitly staged name-bearing object and let Daniel connect it to the scratch. Risk: invents a prop and weakens the voluntary intimacy of an introduction.
evidence: YOU ARE NOT FROM THE EVENING TRAIN.
issues.uncertainty: A generated image might add a name, but no images exist here and unrequested additions cannot supply evidence.
issues.impact: Repair knowledge order before lettering or panel jobs.

issues.title: Counter-to-window movement lacks a stable physical layout
issues.description: The service window is behind the counter and opens into the kitchen, yet later opens between the two men, who are already on opposite sides of a shared counter. No movement explains how both access opposite faces of that window.
issues.why: The exchange boundary is the central action constraint; confusing its location makes safe touch and prohibited crossing hard to read.
issues.preserve: The narrow opening, shared counter, asymmetric damage, and contrast between dangerous and safe contact.
solutions: Approve a simple fixed cafe floor plan and add motivated movement from the counter to the kitchen hatch. Risk: costs a transition beat.
Define the original counter explicitly as the hatch sill and revise the contradictory spatial descriptions in new versions. Risk: changes the opening's established architecture.
evidence: Behind the counter, a narrow service window opened into the kitchen.
Between them, the service window slid open by itself.
- Service Window: Narrow opening between the kitchen and counter.
The narrow service window slides open by itself between the kitchen and counter.
issues.uncertainty: An unusual layout or supernatural relocation could explain this, but neither is established.
issues.impact: Requires geometry-only staging before panel direction; no artwork needed now.

issues.title: The transformation's visible extent is inconsistent in description
issues.description: The prose first says the painted glass clears and broken stools stand upright, then says Daniel's side remains ruined and the painted door still carries the scratch. Page 4 similarly restores objects around Daniel before later split-era staging.
issues.why: Readers need to know whether physical objects restore, an overlay is visible, or only the far side changes, especially when marks become evidence.
issues.preserve: The sensory rush of warmth and the striking split between inhabited past and ruined present.
solutions: Limit restoration to Tomas's visible side and define what Daniel feels across the boundary. Risk: slightly reduces the enveloping miracle.
Keep a transient full-room overlap, explicitly followed by separation. Risk: adds a rule that must remain consistent and may affect later evidence.
evidence: His side of the cafe remained abandoned.
On his side, the name remained scratched into old paint.
Every light in the cafe turns on at once around Daniel.
issues.uncertainty: These passages may describe a subjective overlay, not a factual contradiction; the presentation does not identify it.
issues.impact: Value patterns, damage, and the same objects need stable era states.

issues.title: The reply arrives after the stated exchange interval
issues.description: After 12:07, closure, and several seconds alone, Daniel's notebook page slips from the sealed window with Tomas's reply. The stated exchange rules restrict the reliable connection to seven minutes.
issues.why: This powerful ending can become an unlimited communication loophole unless delayed delivery has a bounded cause.
issues.preserve: I will bring better bread, the smoke-stained aged page, and Daniel's broken laugh.
solutions: Show the paper already caught beneath the closing sill, released seconds later. Risk: makes the wonder more mechanically explicit.
Approve a narrowly defined delayed-return mechanism and track its cost and limits. Risk: adds complexity and invites attempts to bypass the countdown.
evidence: 1. The abandoned railway cafe returns to life

A yellowed notebook page slips from beneath it
issues.uncertainty: Delivery could be physical release rather than a new crossing. The audit does not declare time travel impossible or demand immediate exposition.
issues.impact: A panel must distinguish a caught page from a reopened connection.

issues.title: Object protection and backward adaptation are undefined
issues.description: The rules permit objects to avoid forty years of aging if protected by the interval, but the pastry ages while the interval is active. Backward objects later adapt to the older time, without a defined trigger or physical effect. The preserved note and ordinary notebook page are separate objects.
issues.why: Letters, pastries, photographs, and evidence are the romance and investigation engine. Undefined exceptions let any later outcome seem convenient.
issues.preserve: Asymmetric travel, tactile aging, and archival materials as Daniel's meaningful contribution.
solutions: Specify testable conditions for aging and protection privately, then reveal them through small experiments. Risk: excessive testing could crowd intimacy.
Remove the protection exception from proposed canon and keep consistent forward aging plus ordinary preservation. Risk: restricts future pastry and letter possibilities.
evidence: 5. Objects passed from 1986 to 2026 arrive aged

issues.uncertainty: No demonstrated protective technique or completed post-closure observation of the first sleeve exists.
issues.impact: Each exchange needs before/after state and custody; avoid conflating the two notes.

issues.title: Historical-warning costs need a consistent causal model
issues.description: Direct warnings shorten the connection; coded clues do less damage but the cafe understands intent. Minute loss does not recover easily, implying unspecified recovery. No supplied scene establishes a baseline cost, threshold, or distinction between ordinary flicker and permanent loss.
issues.why: The central dilemma needs consequential choices the reader can learn from. Punishment based on unseen intent risks feeling author-controlled.
issues.preserve: Saving Tomas threatens the means of knowing him; indirect communication should create moral and emotional pressure.
solutions: Approve a private rule matrix with triggers, observables, and recovery limits; dramatize the first measurable loss. Risk: makes a poetic mechanism more constrained.
Retain uncertainty for the characters but establish repeated observable cause/effect for readers. Risk: deliberate ambiguity must still avoid arbitrary exceptions.
evidence: 8. Direct warnings about major historical events

issues.uncertainty: Chapter 1 still reaches 12:07. Its flickers and painful touch are not evidence of a shortened first meeting.
issues.impact: Clock inserts must distinguish elapsed time from lost capacity.

issues.title: Calendar progression and the fire deadline are not yet specified
issues.description: Tomas gives October 17, 1986, and Daniel gives only 2026. The opening says 11:41 PM but does not establish Daniel's calendar date. Notes describe both nightly recurrence and two specific nights; the fire's exact date and how successive meetings advance each era are unavailable.
issues.why: The number of nights before the fire governs rescue urgency, chapter pacing, and whether a long serial can fit the story's clock.
issues.preserve: The forty-year separation and the opening's 12:00-to-12:07 experience.
solutions: Choose paired advancing dates and a defined private fire deadline. Risk: imposes a finite timeline and constrains expansion.
Use deliberately repeated or nonconsecutive past nights, with a consistent mapping rule. Risk: substantially increases reader load and reconstruction scope.
evidence: It is a fragile wound between two specific nights.
1. The abandoned railway cafe returns to life
issues.uncertainty: Do not assume October 17, 2026, an October 17 fire, or equal date advancement. A year offset alone does not establish exact elapsed days.
issues.impact: Every future page needs explicit era/date state where chronology matters.

issues.title: Daniel knows the exact past year before receiving evidence
issues.description: Before Tomas states the year, the close Daniel narration says the kitchen lived in 1986 and that he knew it before proof. His archives are from 1986, but the visible cafe details do not uniquely establish that year.
issues.why: A protagonist defined by evidence loses some credibility when precise knowledge arrives as certainty without a marked intuition.
issues.preserve: Daniel's expertise and the uncanny feeling that the archive has become alive.
solutions: Frame 1986 as a hypothesis tied to the archive, then let Tomas verify it. Risk: slightly softens the lyrical certainty.
Keep the intuition as a deliberate supernatural symptom with later accountable payoff. Risk: adds a new ability or mystery requiring approval.
evidence: Behind the man, the kitchen lived in 1986.
issues.uncertainty: This may be expressive narration rather than literal knowledge; revise only if the intended viewpoint is strict close third.
issues.impact: Use an inference caption only if needed; avoid presenting guessed dates as proven visual labels.

issues.title: The white suit attracts investigative focus without a stated link
issues.description: Daniel singles out the white suit from a list that also includes a failed signal. The opening evidence contains no stated white-suit connection, and Page 11 labels the broker as a suspect or important clue.
issues.why: A fair investigation benefits from a reason for choosing one lead; otherwise the narrative appears to identify the antagonist for Daniel.
issues.preserve: Tomas's observant humor and Daniel missing the compliment while investigating.
solutions: Supply a small existing-record connection before Daniel focuses on the suit. Risk: extra opening information may telegraph the suspect.
Let Daniel ask neutrally about both the broker and signal, with suspicion emerging from later corroboration. Risk: slightly longer exchange.
evidence: A broker in a white suit bought coffee and did not drink it.
Daniel's pencil stopping over the notebook
issues.uncertainty: A conservator can follow a hunch; this is a motivation-strengthening opportunity, not proof of impossible knowledge.
issues.impact: Avoid villain framing that resolves the mystery before evidence does.

Add a precise discrepancy between the archive and the scratch in a future revision. Risk: introduces a new clue that must be approved and tracked.

issues.title: Tomas's independent want is less developed than his rescue function
issues.description: Tomas acts in Chapter 1: he offers bread, asks for a return object, and agrees to meet again. The reference emphasizes his warmth, concealed loneliness, and status as a target, but gives no concrete personal goal that can conflict with Daniel's rescue plan.
issues.why: A long romance needs Tomas to make consequential choices beyond being loved, endangered, or saved.
issues.preserve: His initiative, competence, teasing, chosen family, and bravery under fear.
solutions: Develop an independent obligation or goal from the cafe and notebook material, allowing Tomas to reject a rescue method. Risk: adds plot work and must be approved.
Keep the scope intimate and build his arc through choices about trust, disclosure, and Lilia. Risk: may not support the proposed 105 chapters.
evidence: - Story Function: Gives the cafe its warmth
- Story Function: May have arranged the fire
issues.uncertainty: One opening chapter need not complete his arc; the gap concerns architecture for continuation, not absence of all agency.
issues.impact: Give Tomas observable decisions and work outside Daniel's gaze in later approved scripts.

issues.title: Daniel's emotional need is suggested, while specific grief is unknown
issues.description: Daniel trusts paper more than people, presents I am real, and fears losing the encounter. Notes prescribe adults carrying grief but supply no event explaining his isolation or a particular bereavement.
issues.why: Reconstruction could accidentally invent trauma or reduce his growth to receiving romance. His conflict between preserving evidence and accepting a living person's agency is already stronger material.
issues.preserve: Emotional caution, tactile care, dry humor, and tenderness leaking through professional ritual.
solutions: Build his need around relinquishing control and treating Tomas as a partner; leave personal history understated. Risk: interior change requires precise behavioral beats.
Approve a specific grief history and connect it sparingly to present choices. Risk: risks formulaic backstory and extra exposition.
evidence: Daniel Soriano trusted paper more than people.

issues.uncertainty: Distrust, loneliness, fear of impermanence, and need for connection are interpretations; no deceased lover or family trauma is canon.
issues.impact: Preserve the note and hand acting; do not replace them with explanatory flashbacks by default.

issues.title: The 105-chapter commitment is not supported by developed beats or capacity evidence
issues.description: The series plan recommends seven equal fifteen-chapter arcs and possible expansion to 150 chapters. The available story is one drafted chapter; no scene-level long-series architecture, production capacity, reader feedback, or release calendar is supplied.
issues.why: A numeric target can force delay in the central rescue question and create an unsustainable commitment before the story has earned the length.
issues.preserve: Long-term creative ambition and Daniel/Tomas as the emotional center.
solutions: Treat Arc 1 as a provisional season envelope and validate a small opening sequence before committing beyond it. Risk: changes expectations about the 105-chapter target.
Retain 105 as an aspiration but require each arc to justify new conflict, relationship development, and capacity. Risk: substantial planning burden before release.
evidence: Arc 1 is the opening season and should remain compact at 15 chapters.
issues.uncertainty: No market demand, paid schedule, or author capacity has been validated. No claim that a shorter series sells better is made.
issues.impact: Page count and release frequency remain provisional until production timing and reader checks exist.

issues.title: Other cafes could dilute the specific place and relationship
issues.description: The premise calls the cafe a fragile connection between two specific nights. Arc 4 proposes other seven-minute crossings at abandoned railway sites without a rationale that connects them to Daniel and Tomas's choices.

issues.preserve: San Aurelio Junction as a physical place, emotional anchor, and civic-history mystery.

Defer or remove the multi-cafe expansion from the preferred reconstruction option. Risk: narrows the planned world and total length.

issues.title: Memory-loss and repeat-year arcs need persistent consequences
issues.description: Arc 5 has Tomas no longer remember Daniel clearly, Arc 6 repeats fragments of 1986, and the final arc again asks which future can survive. Without persistent changes, these devices may repeatedly undo earned intimacy.

solutions: Define which consequences and choices survive each alteration; protect Tomas's agency in re-consent. Risk: requires a demanding continuity ledger.
Use one decisive memory rupture near the climax rather than repeated resets. Risk: changes the seven-arc architecture.

may lose every memory made there.
